Hi Martin — thanks for the clear note and the sample invoice. Copying the short version first, then specific notes and next steps.

Short answer (for procurement pack):
- Redwood retains billing records (final invoice PDFs and aggregated usage summaries) for accounting and tax purposes for a minimum of seven years unless otherwise constrained by applicable law. These retained billing artifacts are considered separate business records and are not removed when a customer requests deletion of conversational content.

Details / technical notes:
- Invoice PDFs: These are generated from our billing system and include billing identifiers, period, line-item usage summaries, and the billing contact. They may include customer-provided billing names and email addresses. We can produce redacted copies where billing contact PII (email, address) is masked if required for compliance.
- Aggregated usage summaries: We maintain anonymized or pseudonymized usage aggregates (by customer id and meter) to reconcile charges. These aggregates do not contain raw prompt/response text.
- Raw request/response logs: By default we retain raw request/response logs for operational troubleshooting per the customer plan (typical defaults: 30–90 days for hosted plans). When a verified erasure request is received, we delete raw request/response content per the customer’s instructions, subject to preserving minimal metadata needed to support billing (invoice id, charge amount, timestamp).
- Accounting exceptions: We will preserve minimal billing metadata (invoice id, amount, date, billing entity) even when raw payloads are removed, because that information is necessary for statutory tax records and audit trails.

Attachments I’m including:
- requested_billing_retention_table.xlsx (summary of what we retain, retention windows, redaction options)
- SOC2-summary-2024.pdf (controls overview that covers retention and audit capabilities)

Operational steps if Acme needs us to act on an erasure request while preserving billing records:
1) Customer sends verified erasure request and indicates they need accounting records to be retained.
2) Redwood will delete raw request/response text within 10 business days (subject to verification), and simultaneously create a billing export (PDF + CSV summary) which will be stored in a retention vault for accounting purposes.
3) If Acme requests redaction on the stored invoices (to remove billing contact PII), we can deliver redacted PDFs within 5 business days.
4) If Acme requires a formal attestation or signed statement for procurement, we can produce a one-paragraph attestation and an export package (contains redacted invoice PDF and CSV billing ledger).

If helpful I can draft the exact procurement wording. Karthik — let me know if any of this has commercial implications for the contract (SLAs on turnaround, extra fees for exports).

Thanks,
Laura Bennett
Director, Finance Ops
Redwood Inference
